coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 9 units (the domain directory itself + 8 sub-domain directories, each containing an *-index.md) and 54 files — exactly matching the expected counts. Every file was read in full. Scoring denominator is per-file applicable rubric dimensions summed within each unit (index = 5: dims 1,2,3,7,8; cx = 4: dims 2,3,7,8; feature = 5: dims 1,2,3,7,8). Dimensions 4 (Constraint Explicitness), 5 (Success Measurability) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are N/A throughout this domain — they are owned by meta/constraints.md, meta/problem-statement.md and meta/competitive-landscape.md respectively, which are outside this domain's scope. meta/constraints.md was read only as cited evidence for cross-file contradiction checks, not audited.

findings.claim: Severity tier S0 includes "credible threat" and is hard-routed out of every queue to two destinations that do not handle threats (CSAM and self-harm), leaving credible threats with no reachable adjudication path. The domain CX independently enumerates the bypass set as only three families, none of which is a threat.
findings.evidence: 24.01-reporting-moderation/24.01.03-moderation-queue-reviewer-ops.md:50 — "| S0 | Illegal / imminent-harm (CSAM, credible threat, self-harm) | **Bypasses this queue entirely** — hard-routed to 24.08.01 / 24.06.03; never enters a general lane (DT-04) | Immediate handoff, measured in minutes |". Same file:81 — "Router evaluates the reason family against the skill-map: S0 reasons are hard-routed out to 24.08.01 / 24.06.03 and never touch this queue; all others select a skill-scoped queue (e.g. `sample-clearance`, `credit-dispute`, `gear-authenticity`, `harassment`, `general-policy`)." Same file:176 — "| D-06 | S0-illegal reasons are **structurally** unable to reach a general queue — no code path exists, not merely a rule that forbids it |". Contradicted by trust-safety-disputes-cx.md:208-213 — "Three reason families leave the general queue before any classifier touches them: CSAM (→ 24.08.01, preservation duty), factual rights/credit disputes (→ domains 02/09, wrong remedy …), and **self-harm (→ 24.06.03, no sanction ever)**" — no threat family. 24.08.01 handles CSAM only; 24.06.03 handles self-harm only and forbids any sanction (24.06.03:100 D-02 "No sanction is ever applied to a person in crisis"). Threats are adjudicated in 24.06.01, which is a claim-driven queue case (24.06.01:44-47) that D-06 makes structurally unreachable from an S0 reason.
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent the destination and lifecycle for the most time-critical safety category in the domain: either (a) route credible threats to the `harassment` skill queue, violating D-06's absolute structural exclusion, or (b) hard-route them to 24.06.03, where D-02 forbids any sanction ever — meaning a credible threat can never produce a restriction — or (c) invent a fourth bypass lane that no file defines. All three produce materially different products, and no open question in 24.01, 24.06 or the domain root tracks the choice.

findings.claim: Every sanction at rung 6 or above requires a second, distinct moderator's concurrence and explicitly forbids self-concurrence, while the launch team is a locked constraint of exactly one person — so no account suspension or ban can ever be applied, including the account suspension that the v1 baseline-moderation scope requires.
findings.evidence: 24.02-enforcement-appeals-policy/24.02.01-enforcement-ladder-sanctions.md:178 — "| D-07 | Rung ≥ 6 or `indefinite` duration requires a second moderator's concurrence; no self-concurrence |". Same file:123 — "| **Permission — moderator applies a rung above their authority** (e.g. a rung-7 ban without concurrence) | Rejected as concurrence-required; the proposal is held in `proposed` until a second, distinct moderator concurs. **One person cannot self-concur** |". Rungs 6 and 7 are "Account suspension (time-boxed)" and "Permanent ban" (same file:52-53). Team is locked at one: 24.01-reporting-moderation/24.01.03-moderation-queue-reviewer-ops.md:189 quotes meta/constraints.md § Team verbatim — "**Composition**: **Solo — the owner plus AI agents** (this pipeline and successors). **Implication**: no parallel human workstreams." A model cannot stand in: 24.02-enforcement-appeals-policy/24.02.02-appeals-internal-complaints.md:98 — "| D-03 | The reviewer must not be the original decider, and must not be a model |". And the v1 scope requires the blocked action: 24.01-reporting-moderation/24.01.02-automated-content-classification.md:96 quotes meta/constraints.md § Release Plan — v1 moderation is "(2) an **admin takedown** action (remove content, **suspend account**)".
findings.forcedInvention: A v1 launch must be able to suspend an account (constraints.md) but cannot satisfy D-07's concurrence gate with a one-person team. The implementer must invent one of: an auto-concurrence bypass for the solo case, an AI concurrer (barred by 24.02.02 D-03), a rung-6 exemption from D-07, or a permanently stuck `proposed` state in which no suspension ever lands. 24.01.03 Q-02 tracks only conflict-of-interest recusal and 24.01.03 Q-06's resolution explicitly asserts the opposite — "no routing, exposure, QA or SLA control changes with the answer" — so nothing tracks this.

findings.claim: Every S1 (critical) case is held in `Awaiting concurrence` until a second, independent, unconflicted reviewer concurs, which is unsatisfiable against the locked solo-team constraint — so no S1 sanction (statutory clock, financial harm in progress, active impersonation) can ever land.
findings.evidence: 24.01-reporting-moderation/24.01.03-moderation-queue-reviewer-ops.md:51 — "| S1 | Critical (statutory clock, financial harm in progress, active impersonation) | Skill-routed, priority lane, **two-reviewer concurrence required before sanction** | Shortest human SLA |". Same file:56-57 — "**High-severity (S1) decisions require a second reviewer to concur before the sanction lands.**" Same file:86 — "an S1 decision is held in `Awaiting concurrence` until a second, independent, unconflicted reviewer concurs." Same file:134 — "| Awaiting concurrence | S1 single decision pending a second reviewer | \"Under review\" (concurrence is invisible) |". Against same file:189 (Q-06, RESOLVED) quoting meta/constraints.md § Team — "**Solo — the owner plus AI agents** … **no parallel human workstreams**" — whose resolution text then asserts "The stated scoping holds: no routing, exposure, **QA** or SLA control changes with the answer".
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent what happens to an S1 case when no second reviewer exists — auto-concur, downgrade S1 to S2, waive concurrence below a rung threshold, or leave every critical case permanently un-decided while its statutory clock runs. Q-02 in the same file tracks only conflict-of-interest escalation, not the absence of a concurrer, and Q-06's resolution explicitly denies that any QA control changes.

findings.claim: A CSAM hash match must action the account fully automatically with no human decision in the loop, while the account action it produces is a suspension, which the enforcement ladder makes impossible without a second moderator's concurrence. The two rules cannot both hold.
findings.evidence: 24.08-illegal-content-legal-process/24.08.01-csam-detection-preservation-reporting.md:131 — "| D-01 | Fully automatic on match: block, preserve, report, action — **no human decision** | DT-03 + 24.08 D-02. A decision point is a place where it does not happen. |". Same file:60 — "**Match** → in one automatic transaction, **with no human decision in the loop**: content is blocked and never served, a preservation hold is written, an NCMEC report is filed, and the account is actioned". The action is a suspension: trust-safety-disputes-cx.md:369 — "match → account action proposed → **24.02 applies a generic suspension** → subject sees the standard notice"; 24.08.01:21 — "If actioned, they see only the **generic suspension notice** from 24.02". Suspension is rung 6: 24.02-enforcement-appeals-policy/24.02.01-enforcement-ladder-sanctions.md:52 — "| 6 | Account suspension (time-boxed) | Login-gated action; data stays readable + exportable | Fully |". And rung 6 cannot be applied without a second human: same file:178 — "| D-07 | Rung ≥ 6 or `indefinite` duration requires a second moderator's concurrence; no self-concurrence |"; same file:103 — "If the proposed rung ≥ 6 (suspension or above) … a second moderator's concurrence is required before application; the proposal sits in `proposed` state until concurred or withdrawn".
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent whether the CSAM path bypasses the ladder's concurrence gate (making D-07 conditional, with no rule saying when), or whether a CSAM match leaves the account merely `proposed` and un-suspended pending a second moderator who does not exist. Neither 24.08.01's four open questions nor 24.02.01's four open questions cover the interaction.

findings.evidence: 24.07-identity-abuse-ownership-disputes/24.07.02-entity-ownership-account-recovery-disputes.md:61 — "| An estate claim races an ownership dispute | The worst case; both claims may be legitimate (24.07 CX-02) | `[PENDING]` |". 24.07.03-deceased-incapacitated-succession.md:59 — "| Estate claim races surviving members' ownership claim | Both may be legitimate (24.07 CX-02). **The worst case in the sub-domain** | `[PENDING]` |". 24.07.03:76 — "| Deadlocked | Competing claims | `[PENDING]` |". 24.07.03:57 — "| Band requires unanimous consent; one member is dead | **Governance deadlock.** Nothing can be decided until the estate holds the seat | `[PENDING]` — domain 01's model must anticipate this |". The sub-domain CX calls it live and common: 24.07-identity-abuse-ownership-disputes-cx.md:75-77 — "an estate claim can race an ordinary ownership dispute — surviving band members and an executor claiming the same account, both legitimately. **This is the worst case in the sub-domain and it is not rare.**" Yet every Open Question in the sub-domain is closed: 24.07-identity-abuse-ownership-disputes-index.md Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 are all "✅ Resolved"; 24.07.02 Q-01/Q-02 are "RESOLVED" and Q-03 covers only freeze scoping; 24.07.03 Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 are all "✅ Resolved".
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent the precedence rule when a probate-backed estate claim and a surviving-members mandate claim land on one entity: does the freeze hold both out indefinitely, does probate outrank the mandate graph, does the entity keep accruing to nobody, and who may act in the interim? No file states it, no question tracks it, and the four bare `[PENDING]` cells above carry neither owner nor deferral target — the documented tracking mechanism is absent, not merely deferred.

findings.claim: The evidence locker's `Purged` state row is internally unsatisfiable: it is entered only when every applicable clock has expired, yet its description branches on a financial/evidentiary clock that still applies.
findings.evidence: 24.09-case-evidence-locker.md:144 — "| Purged | **Every applicable clock expired and no hold present** | Nothing; PII anonymised-and-retained **where a financial/evidentiary clock still applies**, fully removed only when all clocks have expired |". The transition guard admits only the first reading: same file:148-149 — "Retained → Purged only when `now ≥ max(all applicable clocks)` **and** no hold — checked atomically at delete time". The anonymise-and-retain branch actually belongs to a different, non-purged situation: same file:79-81 — "A **GDPR erasure request** against a bundle still inside another clock's window resolves to **anonymise-and-retain** … PII fields are tombstoned, financial and evidentiary records are kept."
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must decide whether `Purged` has two variants (a partial anonymise-only purge and a full removal) or whether the anonymise branch is a distinct pre-purge state that the state table omits — which changes the state machine and the deletion job's trigger condition.

findings.claim: CX-09 states three mutually incompatible positions on when the prohibited-items and authenticity gates fire — at checkout, at listing submit, and as pre-publication gates — and its "pre-publication" claim contradicts the owning feature's ratified decision that the engine evaluates twice.
findings.evidence: trust-safety-disputes-cx.md:286 — "Prohibited-items (24.02.05 …) and counterfeit/authenticity (24.05.03 …) both **block a listing at checkout** and must present the seller one coherent reason". Same file:295 — "**Trigger chain**: **listing submit** → both checks run → refusals merged into one message." Same file:297-298 — "**Permission intersection**: none between the two; **both are pre-publication gates**." Contradicted by the owning feature: 24.02-enforcement-appeals-policy/24.02.05-prohibited-restricted-items-engine.md:104 — "| D-02 | The engine evaluates **twice**: listing **and** checkout | DT-02. |", whose DT-02 (same file:85) explicitly rejects the pre-publication-only model: "**restriction is destination-dependent**, so the engine must run at checkout too … A listing-only gate either blocks legal domestic sales … or permits illegal exports".
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must decide at which point(s) the two engines' refusals are merged into the single coherent seller message CX-09 requires: if authenticity is listing-time only (24.05.03 Behavior) and prohibited-items also runs at checkout, the merge is impossible at checkout and CX-09's guarantee holds only at listing — a scope the CX never states.

findings.claim: Two named quality controls — blind independent re-review of a 5% decision sample and forced rotation off high-harm queues — both presuppose at least two reviewers, and are asserted to be unaffected by the now-locked solo-team constraint.
findings.evidence: 24.01-reporting-moderation/24.01.03-moderation-queue-reviewer-ops.md:57-60 — "A configurable sample of all decisions (default 5%, see Q-05) is re-reviewed *blind* for **inter-rater agreement**, because without a measured agreement rate there is no evidence the policy is being applied consistently". Same file:87 — "if the case was in the blind-sampling set, a shadow copy is enqueued for **independent** re-review". Same file:188 (Q-05) — "inter-rater target (Cohen's κ) ≥ 0.7, exposure cap forcing a break after 30 high-harm items or 60 min continuous, **rotation off a high-harm queue every 2 h**". Same file:68-71 (D-02 basis) — "**forced rotation off high-harm queues on a timer** … These controls must be **encoded in the queue regardless of team size**". Against same file:189 — team is "**Solo — the owner plus AI agents** … **no parallel human workstreams**", with the resolution asserting "no routing, exposure, **QA** or SLA control changes with the answer".
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must decide what a "blind, independent" re-review and an "inter-rater" agreement statistic mean when the reviewer and the re-reviewer are the same human, and what "rotation off a high-harm queue" rotates to when there is no other queue-holder. Q-05 offers these as tunable numeric defaults, not as a question about their feasibility.

findings.claim: Report deduplication is specified at two different granularities in two files — by reason code and by reason family — which produces different case counts and different enforcement signals for the same inbound reports.
findings.evidence: 24.01-reporting-moderation/24.01.01-report-intake-notice-and-action.md:60 — "User submits; system dedups against existing open cases on the same **target + reason** within a rolling 30-day window". 24.01-reporting-moderation/24.01-reporting-moderation-cx.md:37-38 — "Two reports on the same target must dedup into one case with N reporters, or a brigade becomes N enforcement signals. Merge strategy: dedup by **(target, reason-family)**, retain each reporter for notification." Reason code and reason family are distinct levels in this domain: routing keys on the family (24.01.03:81 "Router evaluates the **reason family** against the skill-map") while the code is the pinned taxonomy entry (24.01.01:115 "intake must pin the taxonomy version onto each case").
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must choose the dedup key. Under the CX rule two reports of different codes in one family (e.g. "harassment" and "threats") collapse to one case; under the feature rule they do not. That directly changes how many cases a brigade produces — the exact failure mode the CX cites the rule to prevent.

findings.claim: Messaging safety declares that content inspection happens only on report, while the default pre-report signal set requires reading message body text — the boundary between "metadata/pattern" and "content inspection" is never defined, and it is the boundary the feature's own lawful-basis question turns on.
findings.evidence: 24.01-reporting-moderation/24.01.05-messaging-safety-scam-filtering.md:104 — "| D-02 | Default posture is metadata + recipient warning; **content inspection only on report** | DT-01. |". Same file:36-37 — "**Content-level inspection escalates only on report.** A reported thread is evidence …; an unreported thread is not." But the default signal set reads message text: same file:32-34 — "pattern and metadata signals (new account + **first message contains a payment instruction** + off-platform contact + urgency)"; same file:45 — "Metadata/pattern signals evaluate the thread — sender age, prior history, structure, **payment language**"; same file:54 — "| Overpayment cheque scam on gear (\"I'll send £3,000 for the £2,000 amp, wire back the difference\") | Pattern match on **amount-mismatch** + off-platform payment |".
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent where "metadata/pattern" stops and "content inspection" begins — whether the pre-report scanner may read message bodies at all, and if so how deeply. Q-01 asks for the lawful basis "for pattern evaluation of private messages" but presupposes the scope it does not define, so the answer cannot resolve the boundary.

findings.claim: Two concurrence triggers are each stated absolutely and disagree on a reachable case: an S1-severity case resolved at a low rung is simultaneously required to await a second reviewer and to apply immediately.
findings.evidence: 24.02-enforcement-appeals-policy/24.02.01-enforcement-ladder-sanctions.md:104 — "On concurrence (**or immediately, for rungs ≤ 5**), the sanction is applied **atomically** with its Statement of Reasons". Against 24.01-reporting-moderation/24.01.03-moderation-queue-reviewer-ops.md:51 — S1 requires "two-reviewer concurrence **required before sanction**", and same file:86 — "an S1 decision is held in `Awaiting concurrence` until a second, independent, unconflicted reviewer concurs". S1 is defined to include "active impersonation" (24.01.03:51), whose typical remedy is rung 1 content removal or rung 2 feature restriction (24.02.01:47-48) — squarely within "rungs ≤ 5".
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must decide whether the two triggers union (concurrence if either fires) or whether the ladder's rung test is authoritative and the queue's severity test only advisory. Neither file states a precedence, and the choice determines whether every critical case blocks on a second human.

findings.claim: The set of ladder rungs on which `indefinite` duration may be selected is never stated, and the rule that constrains it is not satisfiable alongside the concurrence trigger that presumes it.
findings.evidence: 24.02-enforcement-appeals-policy/24.02.01-enforcement-ladder-sanctions.md:39-40 — "Duration is explicit; `indefinite` is a distinct, higher-severity value, not a default, and **cannot be selected on the same rung as a time-boxed sanction**." The rung table (same file:44-54) declares no duration class for any rung — rung 6 is "Account suspension (**time-boxed**)" and rung 7 "Permanent ban", while rungs 1–4 and 8 state none. Yet the concurrence trigger presumes `indefinite` is reachable below rung 6: same file:103 — "If the proposed rung ≥ 6 (suspension or above) **or** `duration = indefinite`, a second moderator's concurrence is required" — a disjunction that is redundant unless some rung < 6 admits `indefinite`.
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent a per-rung duration allowance table: which of rungs 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 accept `indefinite`, and whether the quoted rule means "a rung is either always time-boxed or always indefinite" or "one sanction record cannot carry both". The two readings produce different validation rules and different concurrence gates.

findings.claim: The sub-domain declares absolutely that it has no sanctioning power and that all friction reaches users through the enforcement ladder with a statement of reasons and an appeal, while its own engine enumerates `block` as a direct outcome and its card-testing feature blocks at the rail with no human, no notice and no appeal.
findings.evidence: 24.03-fraud-risk-operations/24.03-fraud-risk-operations-index.md:67 — "| D-02 | This sub-domain **has no sanctioning power**. It produces signals; 24.02.01 acts | … **All friction lands through the enforcement ladder with an SoR and an appeal.** |". Same file:41-44 — "The four personas experience this sub-domain only as friction — a hold, a block, a verification step — **always** delivered through 24.02.01's sanctions with 24.02.03's reasons". Contradicted by 24.03.01-risk-scoring-rules-engine.md:31 — "the declared outcome — `allow | step-up | hold | review | **block**`" — and same file:69 — "| Block | Rules-certain (card testing, screening hit) | Blocked with a reason |"; and by 24.03.04-triangulation-card-testing-defense.md:28-29 — "Response is **throttle-then-block in milliseconds, before any score is consulted**", same file:44 — "Card testing pattern → throttle → block, **with no human in the loop**", same file:52 — "| 4,000 £0.99 plugin authorisations in 6 minutes across 300 cards | Blocked at the rail … | Attacker: failures. **Nobody else notices** |".
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent the boundary between a "sanction" (which D-02 routes through 24.02 with an SoR and an appeal) and a rail-level "block" (which by construction has neither), and must decide whether a false-positive card-testing block on a legitimate flash-sale buyer produces any notice or redress at all. No decision in 24.03 records the carve-out; 24.03.05 Q-02 tracks only the analogous opacity for screening holds.

findings.claim: The 512(i) repeat-infringer counter's increment timing is stated two incompatible ways in one table: the strike increments only on a notice that was not reversed, yet a reversal is said to decrement a strike that on that reading would never have been created.
findings.evidence: 24.05-copyright-authenticity-enforcement/24.05.01-dmca-notice-counter-notice-repeat-infringer.md:66 — "| Strike N | Counter incremented on a valid notice **not reversed** | Subject sees the count and what the next rung is …". Same file:64 — "| Restored | Business day 10–14 elapses, no suit-filed notice received | Content back; **strike decremented** if the reversal so provides |". Same file:95 — "| Reversal | Reversed strike — appeal upheld (24.02.02) **or counter-notice unopposed through the window** | The counter **must decrement** …". Same file:77 — "The strike counter increments **on the schedule the policy states, automatically and without human discretion**" — a schedule the file never states.
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent whether the counter increments at removal (and decrements on restoration) or only after the 10–14 business-day put-back window closes without a counter-notice. The choice changes what a user's strike count reads during the window and when a termination threshold can trip — on a counter the feature's own DT-01 requires to be "automatic and auditable from launch, precisely so that no human can be shown to have exercised discretion around it". Q-02 defers only the threshold and window values, not the increment event.

findings.claim: A CSAM-driven account action must emit an Art 17 Statement of Reasons whose "facts relied on" field is mandatory, non-empty and honest, while the masking rule forbids the CSAM basis from ever appearing in any SoR — leaving the required field with no permissible content.
findings.evidence: The SoR is mandatory and validated: 24.02-enforcement-appeals-policy/24.02.03-statements-of-reasons.md:76 — "| Required Art 17 field empty at commit (e.g. **facts-relied-on blank**, automated-means null) | SoR generation validation fails → the all-or-nothing unit is refused → **sanction never applies** |"; same file:80 — "| Automated means contributed | **Flag is mandatory and honest** … No null permitted |". The masking rule forbids the only true facts: trust-safety-disputes-cx.md:357-358 — "A CSAM-driven account action surfaces to the subject **only** as 24.02's generic suspension notice; **the CSAM basis is never disclosed in any SoR**"; same file:366-368 — "the enforcement record's user-facing reason field is **deliberately generic** — 24.02 must not leak a CSAM-specific reason into an SoR." This is explicitly framed as an exception to the specificity rule that governs everywhere else: same file:359 — "Specificity is the default everywhere in this domain — here, non-disclosure is mandatory." And the SoR's own edge-case table addresses only reporter-identity withholding (24.02.03:81), never basis withholding.
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent what the facts-relied-on field contains for a CSAM-driven suspension — a generic placeholder that passes non-empty validation but not Art 17's specificity, an omission that trips the validation and blocks the statutorily-mandated account action, or a second SoR class the schema does not define. No open question in 24.08.01, 24.02.03 or the domain root tracks the collision.
